mind_map.root_node: Travelling, Now and Then (5-Digit Numbers, Indian Place Value & Travel Logistics)

key_nodes: Historical Modes: Walking, animal-driven carts, hand-paddled log boats (limited distance range)
Modern High-Speed Modes: Motor boats, diesel/electric trains, highway buses, aviation
Numerical Scale Shift: Scaling daily travel range from single-digit km to 5-digit km magnitudes (up to 99,999 km)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Believing larger physical vehicle size automatically implies higher speed or longer distance travel.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Range Expansion Rule: Transport technological progress increases travel distance capability exponentially.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Comparing historical trade routes with modern national highway networks.

key_nodes: Positional Columns (Right to Left): Ones (O), Tens (T), Hundreds (H), Thousands (Th), Ten Thousands (TTh)
Baseline Magnitude: 10 Thousand = 10,000 (First 5-digit number, 4 zeroes)
Maximum 5-Digit Value: 99,999 (9 Ten Thousands + 9 Thousands + 9 Hundreds + 9 Tens + 9 Ones)
Ten Thousands Period: Grouping (TTh, Th) into thousands period separated by Indian system comma (e.g., 58,042)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Confusing a digit's face value with its positional place value (e.g., in 74,520, face value is 7 but place value is 70,000).
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Place Value = Digit x Column Weight (e.g., 7 x 10,000 = 70,000).
sub_branches.real_world_application: Reading 5-digit population statistics and highway milestone markings.

key_nodes: Additive Decomposition: Expressing numbers as sum of place values (e.g., 67,543 = 60,000 + 7,000 + 500 + 40 + 3)
Predecessor & Successor: Predecessor = Number - 1; Successor = Number + 1
Transition Points: 9,999 + 1 = 10,000 (4-digit to 5-digit boundary)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Omitting zero terms in expanded form notation (e.g., writing 50,402 as 50,000 + 400 + 2 instead of accounting for 0 Thousands).
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Expanded Form = Sum of (Digit x Place Value Weight) for all non-zero digits.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Breaking down bank cheque amounts and financial receipts.

key_nodes: Column-by-Column Comparison: Compare digits from leftmost place (Ten Thousands) to rightmost (Ones)
Greatest Number Formation: Arrange given digits in strict descending order (e.g., digits 3,0,8,5,2 -> 85,320)
Smallest Number Formation: Arrange digits in ascending order, ensuring leading digit is non-zero (e.g., digits 3,0,8,5,2 -> 20,358)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Placing zero as the leading digit when forming smallest n-digit numbers (e.g., 02,358 is a 4-digit value, not 5-digit).
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Comparative Rule: A number with a larger digit in the highest place value column is strictly greater.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Sorting vehicle license plate numbers and highway registration codes.

key_nodes: Nearest Tens Rule: Inspect ones digit; if >= 5, round tens up, else round down
Nearest Hundreds Rule: Inspect tens digit; if >= 5, round hundreds up
Nearest Thousands Rule: Inspect hundreds digit; if >= 5, round thousands up
Logistical Utility: Enables rapid mental estimation for fuel budgets and total travel times
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Rounding down when the decision digit is exactly 5 (5 requires rounding up to higher benchmark).
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Benchmark Rule: Decision digit >= 5 -> Target place incremented by 1; trailing digits set to 0.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Estimating total road trip expenses, fuel volume required, and hotel stays.

key_nodes: Odometer Tracking: Final Odometer Reading - Initial Odometer Reading = Net Distance Covered
Speed Formula: Speed = Distance / Time (e.g., 200 km in 4 hours = 50 km/h)
Distance Formula: Distance = Speed x Time (e.g., 60 km/h for 3.5 hours = 210 km)
Time Formula: Time = Distance / Speed
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Adding initial and final odometer readings instead of subtracting them to find distance.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Distance Delta = Reading_final - Reading_initial; Distance = Speed x Time.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Monitoring commercial bus transit logs, train arrival schedules, and vehicle fuel efficiency.
